overview: Cortex ("Onboarding Brain") is a FastAPI service with a single-page web UI and a Typer CLI. It indexes a local or cloned git repo into a searchable store, then runs Claude Agent SDK agents (chat, guided tour, walkthrough) over the real files with read-only tools. The code lives in `cortex/`: `index/` handles ingestion and retrieval, `agents/` holds the Claude loop and the three agents, and `graph/` does static import analysis. `api/` and `cli/` are thin front doors.

"""Walk a repo and split text/code files into retrievable chunks.

possible, so a retrieved chunk is a coherent unit (a whole function, a whole
README section) and citations land on real symbols instead of arbitrary
character windows. Oversized units fall back to line-aligned windows with
overlap. Bounded: skips heavy/binary dirs and files, caps file size and count.

  index_text — what gets embedded/vectorized (path + text, so file and fo
stops.reason: Decides what text the search index and agents can see.
stops.insight: iter_chunks walks the repo, skipping heavy dirs and lockfiles, and splits at function/class/heading boundaries using per-language regexes. Each chunk carries text, index_text and path/line metadata.

stops.symbol: """Hybrid retrieval: lexical TF-IDF + dense semantic, fused with RRF.
stops.excerpt:
"""Hybrid retrieval: lexical TF-IDF + dense semantic, fused with RRF.

TF-IDF nails exact identifiers ("rate_limit", "TfidfVectorizer"); dense
embeddings bridge vocabulary gaps ("sign in" -> `login`). Reciprocal Rank
Fusion combines both rankings without score calibration: each result
contributes 1/(K + rank) from every list it appears in, so chunks that both
retrievers agree on float to the top. Set ONBOARDING_VECTOR_BACKEND=hybrid.

Costs the dense ingest time (ONNX embedding on CPU), so it suits small/medium
repos; tfidf remains the fast default.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

impo
stops.reason: The optional semantic backend, showing how the store interface is extended.
stops.insight: HybridStore combines TfidfStore and DenseStore results using reciprocal rank fusion (rrf_merge). It skips dense embedding above hybrid_max_chunks so large repos stay fast.

stops.symbol: """The agent loop — the ONE place Cortex runs Claude as an agent.
stops.excerpt:
"""The agent loop — the ONE place Cortex runs Claude as an agent.

`run_tool_agent()` runs a Claude Agent SDK tool-use loop over the repo's files:

    Python                                     Claude (via the SDK + Claude Code CLI)
    ──────                                     ──────────────────────────────────────
    query(prompt, options) ──────────────────▶ reads the question
                                               picks a tool  ──┐
    PreToolUse hook  ◀──── "Grep(...)" ────────────────────────┘
      outside the repo?  → denied
    tool runs (Read / Grep / Glob / search_code)
stops.reason: The single place where an agent actually runs. Chat, tour and walkthrough all call it.
stops.insight: run_tool_agent sets up Read/Grep/Glob plus the in-process search_code MCP server. PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks (_fence_hooks) block paths outside the repo and record seen files. resolve_indexed_path drops invented paths.

stops.symbol: """The chat agent — answers one question about an indexed repo.
stops.excerpt:
"""The chat agent — answers one question about an indexed repo.

    ask(question)
      │  "hi" / "thanks"?  → canned reply, Claude is not called
      │  prompt = last 6 chat turns + the question
      ▼
    loop.run_tool_agent(CHAT_SYSTEM_PROMPT, prompt, CHAT_SCHEMA, max 12 turns)
      │  Claude searches and reads the code (Read/Grep/Glob/search_code), then
      │  answers in CHAT_SCHEMA's shape: {found, answer, sources[path, lines]}
      ▼
    _build_response()
      │  found = false  → no sources, grounded = False
      │  otherwise sources = the files Claude cited, kept only if indexe
stops.reason: Backs /v1/ask and /v1/ask/stream, the core Q&A feature.
stops.insight: ask() short-circuits small talk and builds a prompt from recent history, then runs the loop with CHAT_SCHEMA. _grounded_sources keeps only cited files that are indexed and were read. It attaches wiring and saves chat history.
